query: What causes porosity in MIG welding and how do I prevent it?
rationale: kb:porosity is the primary defect entry detailing low gas flow, drafts, surface contaminants, and voltage/travel speed remedies. doc:shielding_gas_selection.md#4 covers flow rate bounds (15-20 L/min), drafts, leaking lines, and diffusers as root causes of porosity.

query: Why am I getting undercut at the weld toe and how can I fix it?
rationale: kb:undercut explains current/voltage too high, excessive travel speed, and incorrect torch drag angle, recommending lower parameters and weave dwell.

query: How do I resolve lack of fusion between weld passes or on the sidewall?
rationale: kb:lack_of_fusion addresses insufficient heat input, poor joint prep/gap, and improper arc direction against joint sidewalls.

query: Why is my GMAW process producing excessive spatter?
rationale: kb:spatter identifies low voltage for wire speed, high-CO2 gas mixtures, excessive stick-out, and recommends Ar-rich gas and voltage trimming.

query: How can I prevent angular distortion and warpage on thin stainless steel weldments?
rationale: kb:distortion focuses on high heat input, low thermal conductivity in stainless, back-step sequencing, fixturing, and copper chill bars.

query: What welding parameter adjustments prevent burn through on thin sheet metal?
rationale: kb:burn_through details current reduction, faster travel speed, short-circuit or pulsed transfer, and backing bars to avoid excessive heat input.

query: What is the difference between hot solidification cracking and cold hydrogen cracking?
rationale: kb:cracking explicitly contrasts solidification (hot) cracking from impurities and bead shape against hydrogen (cold) cracking from moisture and delayed embrittlement.

query: What causes delayed cracking after cooling in high-strength steel welds?
rationale: kb:cracking explicitly notes that cracking appearing after cooling (delayed) is classic hydrogen cold cracking requiring pre-heat and low-hydrogen consumables.

query: Why is the weld bead profile too narrow and ropey instead of flat and wetted?
rationale: kb:narrow_bead explains voltage too low, tight arc cone, excessive stick-out, and why voltage should be adjusted first to increase bead width and wetting.

query: How to prevent dark blue discoloration and loss of corrosion resistance on stainless steel?
rationale: kb:discoloration describes heat-tint oxide colors, chromium depletion, reduced heat input, back-purging with argon, and pickling/passivation.

query: What causes penetration to vary inconsistently along the length of a weld seam?
rationale: kb:inconsistent_penetration identifies variable root gaps, manual speed variance, feeder instability, and heat buildup along continuous seams.

query: How can an engineer maximize weld joint tensile strength?
rationale: kb:tensile_strength explains that tensile strength relies on full fusion, defect-free metal, matched/over-matched filler, and avoiding excessive heat input.

query: What welding parameters produce a clean, uniform bead appearance with fine ripples?
rationale: kb:bead_appearance details balancing voltage against wire-feed/current, steady travel, Ar-rich gas, and pulsed MIG transfer for TIG-like ripple cosmetics.

query: Why does heavy sugaring or severe heat tint appear on the backside of stainless welds?
rationale: kb:discoloration explicitly addresses dark blue/grey sugaring on the back of stainless as chromium-depleted oxide resulting from inadequate root back-purging.

query: What is the recommended heat input range in kJ/mm for austenitic stainless steel?
rationale: kb:heat_input_range recommends keeping stainless heat input roughly 0.5-1.5 kJ/mm to prevent sensitisation and distortion.

query: What are the primary operational parameters that act as dominant quality drivers in welding?
rationale: kb:quality_drivers maps the five core levers: heat input, current/wire-feed, voltage, travel speed, and shielding gas flow/type.

query: How does travel speed interact with current and voltage to determine heat input?
rationale: Both passages outline heat input as (I * V / S) and discuss how travel speed balances penetration against distortion and HAZ degradation.

query: Which parameter should be adjusted first to increase weld bead width and improve toe wetting?
rationale: kb:narrow_bead and kb:quality_drivers note that arc voltage chiefly controls bead width, wetting, and toe contact angles.

query: How does excessive contact-tip-to-work stick-out distance cause arc instability and spatter?
rationale: kb:spatter and kb:narrow_bead identify improper stick-out (recommending 10-15 mm) as a prime driver of arc instability, high spatter, and ropey bead shapes.

query: How can a welding shop increase the metal deposition rate in kilograms per hour?
rationale: kb:deposition_increase outlines wire-feed speed, wire diameter, spray/pulsed-spray transfer, and metal-cored or flux-cored consumables.

query: What methods are most effective to reduce total welding cycle time and arc-off non-productive time?
rationale: kb:minimize_time emphasizes that arc-on time is <30% of cycle time, pointing to fixturing, fewer passes, spatter reduction, and cutting defect rework.

query: Which welding process offers the best productivity and deposition balance for 5mm stainless plate?
rationale: kb:process_productivity compares MIG/GMAW (especially pulsed spray) against TIG and SMAW, recommending pulsed MIG for 5mm stainless plate.

query: How can manufacturing plants systematically reduce rework and post-weld grinding?
rationale: kb:reduce_rework outlines qualified WPS lockdown, clean edge preparation, fit-up accuracy, and robotic repeatability to eliminate defects upstream.

query: How can shielding gas consumption and expenses be reduced without risking weld porosity?
rationale: kb:gas_consumption explains setting optimal flow (12-18 L/min), installing surge gas-savers, fixing line leaks, and eliminating drafts.

query: How does wire spatter loss and deposition efficiency affect overall consumable cost per meter?
rationale: kb:consumable_cost analyzes deposition efficiency, wire spatter waste, solid vs metal-cored wire tradeoffs, and total labor-dominated cost structures.

query: What cost component represents the dominant fraction of total weld manufacturing cost?
rationale: kb:manufacturing_cost highlights that labor and overhead comprise 70-85% of total weld cost, demonstrating why arc-on time and first-time-right quality dominate material costs.

query: What are the four primary levers to improve overall welding fabrication efficiency?
rationale: kb:improve_efficiency names the four levers: arc-on duty cycle, deposition rate, defect/rework reduction, and consumable waste elimination.

query: What shielding gas blend is recommended for MIG welding stainless steel?
rationale: Both sources recommend Ar-rich tri-mixes (Ar/He/CO2 or Ar/2%CO2) and explain why CO2 must remain low (<= 2-3%) to prevent sensitization and carbide precipitation.

query: What shielding gas mixture should be chosen for GMAW of carbon and mild steel?
rationale: Both sources detail pure CO2 vs Ar-20%CO2 vs Ar-8%CO2, contrasting penetration, spatter levels, and spray transfer capability.

query: Can CO2 or oxygen be used in shielding gas mixtures when MIG welding aluminum?
rationale: doc:shielding_gas_selection.md#3 explicitly cautions never to use CO2 or oxygen on aluminum because they violently oxidise the weld pool causing severe dross and porosity.

query: What is the recommended shielding gas flow rate in L/min for standard GMAW MIG welding?
rationale: doc:shielding_gas_selection.md#4 specifies 15-20 L/min, consistent with kb:porosity (15-20 L/min) and kb:gas_consumption (12-18 L/min).

query: Why should CO2 content in stainless steel shielding gas be kept below 2 to 3 percent?
rationale: Both documents explain that carbon pickup from higher CO2 concentrations causes carbide precipitation in the HAZ, destroying corrosion resistance.

query: Why does an excessively high shielding gas flow rate cause weld porosity rather than preventing it?
rationale: Both passages highlight that excessive gas velocity generates turbulent aspiration that sucks atmospheric oxygen and nitrogen into the molten weld pool.

query: What are the operating requirements and physical characteristics of spray transfer in GMAW?
rationale: kb:transfer_mode covers current thresholds (>150-200A), Ar-rich gas requirement (>=80%), flat/horizontal position limitation, and deep penetration / low spatter dynamics.

query: When should pulsed MIG welding be chosen instead of short-circuit or spray transfer?
rationale: Both passages explain that pulsed MIG combines spray-like low spatter and deposition with all-position capability and lower average heat input for distortion-prone stainless.

query: What minimum current and argon percentage are required to achieve spray arc?
rationale: kb:transfer_mode explicitly notes spray requires >~150-200 A and ~80%+ argon.

query: What DAQ hardware is required to sample high-rate analog arc voltage and current signals at 10 kHz?
rationale: kb:sensor_hardware_daq specifies NI cDAQ with NI-9215 (voltage) and NI-9227 (current) or NI USB-6363 sampling at >=10 kHz alongside PTP IEEE 1588 synchronization.

query: How does robot seam-finding touch sensing and closed-loop force-torque control maintain seam tracking?
rationale: kb:robot_kinematics_control explains touch-sense seam finding, wrist F/T contact force, and depth standoff feedback loops.

query: How is the weld process simulated in Isaac Sim given that arc metallurgy and weld pools are not modeled?
rationale: kb:weld_process_simulation explains modeling the weld as a kinematic trajectory + contact event, using scripted scenario variables (I, V, speed) validated against physics formulas.

query: What ROS 2 topics and topic contract allow seamless sim-to-real transfer to physical robot hardware?
rationale: kb:sim_to_real_digital_twin defines the ROS 2 topic contract over /wrist/rgb, /wrist/depth, /cell/scan, /weld/ft, and /weld/params.
